extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies, regulated entities, attorneys, stakeholders, and members of the public who read Federal Register notices and participate in rulemaking or advisory committee meetings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and requirements for Federal Register publications, accessing rulemaking dockets and incorporated materials, attending and submitting public comments at federal advisory/agency meetings, and statutory/regulatory criteria referenced in notices (e.g., tobacco market designation, SAH grant indexing).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to cite this publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the volume number and the page number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided on page: "Use the volume number and the page number. Example: 90 FR 12345."

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inspection of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents are on file for public inspection in the Office of the Federal Register the day before they are published, unless the issuing agency requests earlier filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a list of documents currently on file for public inspection, see www.federalregister.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: No restrictions on republication
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no restrictions on the republication of material appearing in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription / electronic Table of Contents mailing list
rubrics_metrics.description: How to subscribe to the Federal Register Table of Contents electronic mailing list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction: "To subscribe to the Federal Register Table of Contents electronic mailing list, go to https://public.govdelivery.com/accounts/USGPOOFR/subscriber/new, enter your e-mail address, then follow the instructions to join, leave, or manage your subscription." Notes that FEDREGTOC is a mailing list only and staff cannot respond to specific inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing and examining rulemaking dockets (example: FAA AD docket)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dockets (e.g., AD docket) are available electronically and for in-person inspection under stated conditions and contain the rule, supporting information, and comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example wording: "You may examine the AD docket at regulations.gov under Docket No. 2024-2661; or in person at Docket Operations between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays. The AD docket contains this final rule, the mandatory continuing airworthiness information (MCAD), any comments received, and other information." Also describes where to obtain material incorporated by reference (EASA contact details, FAA Airworthiness Products Section address) and that such material is available at regulations.gov under the docket number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA) meeting notice and public access
rubrics_metrics.description: Meetings of advisory committees are announced under FACA, include stated purpose, date/time/location, and are open to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) gives notice under the Federal Advisory Committee Act, 5 U.S.C. ch. 10, the VA National Academic Affiliations Council (NAAC) will meet via conference call on June 18, 2025... The meeting is open to the public. The purpose of the Council is to advise the Secretary..."

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral public comment procedures for the VA NAAC meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules for members of the public wishing to make oral comments at the specified VA advisory committee meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key requirements and guidance from the notice: "The Council will receive oral public comments from 2:25 p.m. to 2:55 p.m. EST. Interested persons may attend and present oral statements to the Council on June 18, 2025, during the public comment period. The designated public dial in is 872 701 0185. At the prompt, enter meeting ID 744 975 227#. Individuals who speak are invited to submit a 1- to 2-page summary of their comments at the time of the meeting for inclusion in the official meeting record. Oral presentations will be limited to five minutes or less, depending on the number of participants. Interested parties may also provide written comments for review by the Council prior to the meeting to Ms. Nellie Mitchell... or at any time via email to Nellie.Mitchell@va.gov. Any member of the public wishing to attend or seeking additional information should contact Ms. Mitchell via email or by phone at 608-358-9902."

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for referendum before designating tobacco auction markets (Tobacco Inspection Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before any tobacco auction market is designated, the Secretary must determine by referendum the desire of tobacco growers who sold tobacco at auction on that market during the preceding marketing season.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As stated: "Under the Tobacco Inspection Act (7 U.S.C. 511d), the Secretary is authorized to designate those auction markets... It also provides that, before any market is designated, the Secretary is required to determine by referendum the desire of tobacco growers who sold tobacco at auction on such market during the preceding marketing season." The notice documents that a simple majority vote of eligible producers was necessary to terminate designations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of tobacco market designation: mandatory inspection/certification
rubrics_metrics.description: If a tobacco market is designated by the Secretary, tobacco may not be offered for sale at auction on that market until it has been inspected and certified by an authorized representative of the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact phrasing from the notice: "Once tobacco markets are designated by the Secretary, no tobacco may be offered for sale at auction on such market until it has been inspected and certified by an authorized representative of the Secretary."

rubrics_metrics.name: USDA policy preference re: obsolete regulations and deregulatory focus
rubrics_metrics.description: When uncertain about costs and benefits of regulations, USDA policy is to favor deregulation and focus resources on enforceable, discrete regulations; this can justify rescinding obsolete regulations lacking reliance interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the preamble: "To the extent there is any uncertainty about the costs and benefits of these regulations, it is the policy of USDA to err on the side of deregulation and focus resources on fairly and rationally enforcing a discrete and manageable number of regulations. USDA has determined that there is no reliance interest in the regulations to be removed. Moreover, regardless of the lawfulness, USDA has no interest in maintaining a regulation that is unnecessary for the reasons stated above. The regulations in subpart D of 7 CFR part 29 are not a priority."

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for adjusting SAH grant aggregate amounts (VA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory method for annual adjustment of Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) grant amounts using the Turner Building Cost Index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As stated in the notice: "Section 2102(e)(2) authorizes the Secretary to increase the aggregate amounts of SAH assistance annually based on a residential home cost-of construction index. The Secretary uses the Turner Building Cost Index for this purpose... Such increase will be equal to the percentage by which the Turner Building Cost Index for the most recent calendar year (CY) exceeds that of the next preceding CY. If... the Turner Building Cost Index for the most recent full CY is equal to or less than the next preceding CY, the percentage increase will be zero." The notice further explains the selection of second-quarter-to-second-quarter comparison for timeliness and provides resulting FY2025 percentages and dollar amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket material availability and in-person inspection hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Docket materials may be inspected electronically or in person during specified hours and locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "You may examine the AD docket at regulations.gov under Docket No. 2024-2661; or in person at Docket Operations between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays. The address for Docket Operations is U.S. Department of Transportation, Docket Operations, M–30, West Building Ground Floor, Room W12-140, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC 20590."

rubrics_metrics.name: How to obtain materials incorporated by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact details and locations for obtaining materials that are incorporated by reference into a final rule (example: EASA materials and FAA viewing location).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example instructions: "For EASA material identified in this AD, contact EASA, Konrad-Adenauer-Ufer 3, 50668 Cologne, Germany; telephone +49 221 8999 000; email ADs@easa.europa.eu. You may find this material on the EASA website at ad.easa.europa.eu. You may view this material at the FAA, Airworthiness Products Section, Operational Safety Branch, 2200 South 216th St., Des Moines, WA... It is also available at regulations.gov under Docket No. FAA–2024–2661."
